title: fix(gateway): operator Stop misses OpenAI-compatible HTTP runs before the runner starts
body:
Related: #168080 (follow-up to its "Not covered" note)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: operator Stop (`chat.abort { sessionKey }`, TUI Esc, `sessions.abort { key }`) does nothing when it arrives in the first seconds of an OpenAI-compatible HTTP run, even though `sessions.list` already shows the session as running. The request goes on to the provider and the HTTP client gets a normal answer later.

## User Impact

User impact: Stop now stops a run started without a Gateway chat controller, such as `POST /v1/chat/completions` or `POST /v1/responses`, from the moment it is admitted, including while it is still queued for its session. The waiting HTTP request ends right away with `500 "agent run was cancelled"` and the provider is never called. `chat.abort` returns the run id in `runIds`, and `sessions.abort` returns it as `abortedRunId`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168080 made the shared session Stop plan stop controller-less runs, but only through the embedded run handle. The runner registers that handle just before it calls the provider, yet the run is already admitted and shown as active well before then. On a loaded host the gap measured 0.6 to 12 s. A Stop in that window found no owner: live, `chat.abort` answered `aborted: false, runIds: []` and `sessions.abort` answered `no-active-run`.

The command already holds the right owner for that window. `agentCommandInternal` reserves a session-work admission before it waits and before the run registry projects it, and keeps it until cleanup. That admission's interrupt already aborts the command's lifecycle controller.

This change lets the admission declare which run it belongs to. The shared Stop plan then uses a targeted capture to interrupt exactly that run, and credits the stop only when the owner returns its `{ runId }` receipt. The Gateway `agent` RPC admission already follows that receipt contract. Right before the side effect, the capture rechecks that the admission is still live, not already interrupted, and in the current lifecycle generation, so a delayed Stop cannot land on a released or replacement run. Run liveness stays with the agent-run registry; no abort handles were added there or to the embedded run registry.

The existing selection rules carry over:
- The embedded handle stays the preferred owner once it exists.
- Controller-backed runs stop only through their controller.
- Narrow `operator.sessions.write` callers only reach their admitted incarnation.
- Internal and subagent-coordination runs stay hidden, using the same visibility fact the run registry uses.
- Exact-`runId` and `global` requests never take this path.
- Like the embedded stop, the admitted-run stop only runs for callers that opt in with `stopEmbeddedRun` (`chat.abort`, `sessions.abort`, archive/delete drain). The `chat.send` `/stop` pre-admission path, worker placement cancel, and queued-collector Stop leave these runs alone, as they do on `main` today.

Three read-only admission queries moved unchanged into the existing queries module to keep `session-lifecycle-admission.ts` under its line cap.

Release-note context: user-visible fix to session Stop for OpenAI-compatible HTTP and other controller-less runs while they are admitted or queued, before the runner starts.

## Evidence

**Final validation.** [CI run 38075524838](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38075524838) completed successfully on exact head `b6268d9d057d4fbb536f61d5fd17155ea385228a`: 76 jobs, all success or skipped, 495 s elapsed. The affected attachment test also passes on Node 24 on this head (1 passed, 76 skipped; 75.18 s wall). No skipped or earlier cancelled check is counted as passing proof. No CI rerun or inherited-failure admin exception was used.

**Attachment-test refresh.** The head used by [run 38073945128](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38073945128) passed the focused local Stop proof (43/43 on Node 24; 436.08 s combined wall), but CI stopped at the unchanged duplicate-attachment parsing-race fixture in `server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`: its dispatch call count was asserted immediately after admission. Main already carried `d1dc0c1c76dd`, which waits for the real dispatch-entry signal and preserves the ACK, dedupe, registration, and cleanup assertions; its commit records Linux proof of the original 236-test shard. Merged `main` at `be67cc961afd` to incorporate that fix, producing `b6268d9d057d`. The merge was conflict-free and changed none of the Stop implementation files. Exact final-head CI is successful as recorded above; no admin exception or CI rerun was used.

**Refresh after the inherited lint failure.** Merged `main` at `e3dad3b6100bcbbf3ce3b53f5e8af85995fdff9b`, which contains `493a499b86e3` (the cleanup-release consistent-return fix), producing head `18afc82b6921`. The merge was conflict-free and changed none of the three Stop implementation files. Fresh CI and the focused Node 24 command/authority tests are running on this head. The prepared inherited-failure exception is not being used.

**Prior CI failure attribution.** On `acca701895f8`, [CI run 38071906921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38071906921) has one failed leaf: [changed lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38071906921/job/114271521943). Its full log reports:
```text
scripts/lib/managed-cleanup-handoff.mts:224:9: error: Function 'release' expected no return value. (typescript(consistent-return))
```
The remaining cancelled jobs were stopped by the successful `pr-fail-fast` monitor; `openclaw/ci-gate` reports the same originating failure. This file, its lint configuration, and the script-lint runner are outside this PR's diff. The same error appears in the [latest hourly main run 38072014174, check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38072014174/job/114271424536), based on the same `2cd5dea12c86` main commit, and reproduces with the targeted script-lint command on current main `b96c661becbc`. This is an inherited tooling-lint failure, not a failing Stop test. Resolved by merging main through the fix described above; no inherited-failure admin exception was used. No cancelled check is claimed as passing.

**CI repair: first cancellation reason on Node 24.** The first refreshed run, [38069034199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38069034199), failed the new visible and coordination command-interruption cases and fail-fast cancelled the remaining jobs. This was a real runtime issue: on Node 24.21.0, an unread `AbortSignal.any()` reason can change when a second source aborts. The same two-controller reproducer retains the first reason on Node 26. The command now forwards parent cancellation into its existing lifecycle controller, retaining one stable reason, and disposes that listener with the command. The original first-interruption assertions are unchanged.

The original failing infra file order (`agent-command.restart-settlement.test.ts` plus `agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts`) reproduced 2 failures on Node 24 before the fix (501.81 s wall), then passed 31/31 after it (373.02 s wall). The three command-admission cases also passed on Node 26 (155.05 s wall). Node 24 recovery-owner, admitted-Stop, and pending-admission checks passed 72/72 (392.38 s combined wall). Agent-root types, core lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI on the repaired head is pending.

**Refresh.** Merged `main` at `f9371958b137ec885ec0e53551755894ec48598f` to pick up #168328's Details fix after the first CI run hit that red-main window. The only conflict was documentation; the resolution retains both the current typed-/stop explanation and this PR's admitted-run wording.

- **Authority boundaries.** Five production-RPC cases now exercise real declared admissions with no embedded handle: forbidden callers cause no interruption and leave the row unchanged with the session-not-found response; allowed callers interrupt once with a direct-abort reason and persist the killed/aborted run before success; revocation from the queued-turn signal prevents admitted interruption; revocation inside the admitted interruption prevents its cancellation write; and revocation by the first of two admitted owners prevents the second owner's callback and controller abort. Revoked cases leave the row unchanged and assert the exact revocation/aggregate error shape. **Bite proof:** removing only the per-iteration `params.assertCurrent?.()` in the admitted loop makes the two-admission case fail because the second interruption is called once (1 failed, 11 skipped; 65.69 s wall). Restoring it passes all 12 tests (107.28 s wall). The original queued-revocation case stays green under that narrower mutation because earlier plan guards already reject it; the two-admission case specifically proves the loop guard. No timers, sleeps, polling, or new Gateway boots were added.

**Validation after refresh.** `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-admitted.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 12/12 passed. The combined `chat-send-pre-admission.test.ts` and `sessions.abort-embedded.test.ts` run passed 51/51 in 108.40 s wall. The gateway-methods test type check passed in 31.16 s after updating this checkout's dependencies to the frozen lockfile; the earlier local Google type errors came from an older installed dependency. Changed-file format, core oxlint, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Earlier-head measurements below remain historical evidence; CI seconds for this refreshed head are pending.

**Real Gateway, before and after.** Isolated QA Gateway child (`createQaGatewayChild`, mock OpenAI provider, both HTTP endpoints enabled). Stop is sent as soon as `sessions.list` shows the row with `hasActiveRun: true, status: "running"`, and before the mock's `/debug/inflight-requests` lists the request. "Before" is #168080's head, built; "after" is this branch rebased on `main` `e67e13cf1e2a` and rebuilt.

| Case (early Stop) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` + `chat.abort` ×3 | `{ aborted: false, runIds: [] }`; provider got the request 0.66–12.3 s later; request still pending 30 s after Stop | `runIds: ["chatcmpl_…"]`; `500 "agent run was cancelled"` 128–2446 ms after Stop; provider never called; row cleared |
| `/v1/chat/completions` + `sessions.abort` ×2 | `{ status: "no-active-run", abortedRunId: null }`; still pending | `{ status: "aborted", abortedRunId: "chatcmpl_…" }`; 500 in 546–1660 ms; provider never called |
| `/v1/responses` + `chat.abort` | `{ aborted: false, runIds: [] }`; still pending | `runIds: ["resp_…"]`; 500 in 715 ms; provider never called |
| Control: Stop after the provider has the request | stopped (#168080 path) | still stopped, 147 ms |

The same driver had already passed 7/7 on the pre-rebase head, with early Stops settling in 84–734 ms.

**Regressions.**
- `sessions.abort-admitted.test.ts`: `chat.abort`/`sessions.abort stops an admitted controller-less run before its embedded handle exists`. These run inside a real session-work admission and `withExecRequestTurn`, with no embedded handle. On the base, with only the production diff reverted, they fail with `runIds: []` instead of `["http-admitted-run"]` and `abortedRunId: null` instead of the run id. Five boundary cases: a controller-backed run (controller aborted exactly once, admission untouched), an old incarnation for a narrow caller, an already-aborted owner (no receipt, original reason kept), a hidden run, and a missing session id.
- `chat-send-pre-admission.test.ts`: a non-opt-in `/stop` leaves both an admitted and an embedded controller-less producer untouched. With the `stopEmbeddedRun` gate removed it fails (`aborted: true, runIds: ["admitted-producer"]`).
- `agent-command.restart-settlement.test.ts`: drives the real `agentCommandFromGatewayIngress` for visible, internal, and coordination runs. The command declares its identity, observes Stop before model selection, never reaches the attempt, and issues its receipt only once.
- `session-lifecycle-admission.pending.test.ts`: capture revalidation (released, interrupted, retired generation, undeclared, caller's own stack, wrong receipt), plus stopping a queued declared run without touching its predecessor.

**Suites on the rebased head.** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, all passing (wall time on a host at load 60–95):

| File | Passed | Wall |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.abort-admitted` | 7 | 557 s |
| `agent-command.restart-settlement` | 24 | 721 s |
| `session-lifecycle-admission.pending` | 16 | 21 s |
| `session-lifecycle-admission` | 30 | 166 s |
| `sessions.abort-embedded` | 25 | 414 s |
| `sessions.abort-agent-scope` | 30 | 116 s |
| `chat.abort-persistence` | 29 | 151 s |
| `chat.abort-errors` | 13 | 313 s |
| `chat-send-pre-admission` | 26 | 139 s |
| `server-worker-placement-cancel` | 3 | 366 s |
| `agent-run-execution-phase.owner` | 31 | 164 s |
| `inference-lifecycle-caller` | 4 | 119 s |
| `sessions-mutations.archive-attribution` | 13 | 158 s |
| `worker-turn-launcher` | 36 | 599 s |

Before the rebase, the remaining #168080 Stop suites and the subagent-control suites that read interruption receipts also ran: 315/315. The new tests reuse suite fixtures and add no timers, sleeps, polling, or Gateway boots. CI seconds: pending this PR's run.

**Checks.** These pass: format, targeted oxlint, line-cap ratchet, config docs, and `git diff --check`. The gateway-methods and agents-root test type graphs report only two `google-stream.ts` errors that also occur on `main`. `check-changed` and the full type passes stop on three failures that reproduce on the exact base `e67e13cf1e2a`:
- a stale `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` entry for `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts`
- `TS2769`/`TS2353` in `packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts` (`FinishReason` lacks `CONTINUATION`)
- six `TS2307` errors for `@openclaw/crabbox-provider/cli-runtime-api.js` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/*`

`$autoreview` (Codex): scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the pre-rebase diff and again on this rebased branch against its merge base.

**Not covered / follow-ups.**
- Cron and hook runs call `runEmbeddedAgent` directly instead of `agentCommand`, so they keep the late-handle window.
- A foreground-maintenance wait before the command's admission is also outside this window.
- Plugin-runtime, node-event, and TUI ingress share the fixed command owner but were not exercised live.
- `chat.send` `/stop` still does not stop controller-less runs at all. That is a #168080 design choice (no live-authority owner on that path), unchanged here.
